summary.headline: Harsha Engineers Q2 FY27: consolidated Engineering revenue INR428 crores (+18% YoY) and EBITDA INR81.1 crores; India growth above 24%, Romania being downsized.
summary.overview: Management described Q2 as business as usual and largely on track, with India Engineering revenue up over 24% YoY and H1 up about 23%. Consolidated Engineering revenue reached INR428 crores versus INR363 crores a year earlier, and consolidated EBITDA margin rose to about 18.6%, helped by metal pass-through, lower solar mix and operational efficiency. Management reaffirmed full-year FY27 guidance of mid-to-high teens India growth and 10-12% consolidated growth, but stressed it is conservative given metal-price inflation and a planned Romania downsizing. Romania downsizing details, capex timing and Advantek losses remained open items for next quarter.

segments.name: India Engineering (Cages, Bushings, Stampings)
segments.commentary: Revenue up over 24% YoY in Q2 and 23% in H1, with growth across Cages, Bushings and Stampings. Management guides India growth in the mid-to-high teens for FY27 and an EBITDA margin around 22% steady state.

segments.name: Bushings
segments.commentary: Management expects about 30% growth in FY27, driven by windmill gearbox customers, with a long-term target of about INR300 crores in three to four years. One new-contract commercialisation is seen as slightly delayed but still expected.

segments.name: Stampings
segments.commentary: Expects over 30% growth in FY27 versus about INR72 crores in FY26, with the accumulator product launched recently; long-term target about INR300 crores over four years. Management said it may bring forward the INR150-200 crore run-rate milestone.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Q2 revenue INR11.9 crores and EBITDA INR0.73 crores. FY27 and FY28 guidance is INR150-200 crores, dependent on government import and subsidy norms, which are viewed as cyclical.

segments.name: China
segments.commentary: Sequentially softer versus Q1 but up YoY; current-portfolio growth estimated at 5-7%, with EBITDA margin in single digits. New capacity targeted for Q2-Q3 FY28.

segments.name: Romania
segments.commentary: Management is downsizing operations and cutting costs, aiming to arrest operating losses by end FY27. FY28 revenue expected to be lower but still positive for profitability; details to come in about one quarter.

segments.name: Harsha Advantek (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 loss about INR7 crores versus about INR12 crores a year earlier. FY27 revenue guidance INR140 crores or slightly higher; H2 expected to be profit positive. Standalone-to-consolidated gap is about INR12 crores loss, with foreign subsidiaries' Q2 loss INR1.7 crores.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth reaffirmed at 10-12%; India Engineering growth mid-to-high teens; management said guidance is conservative given metal inflation and Romania downsizing.
Global volume growth target of 12-15% for the company; Q2 pass-through estimated at 4-5% of H1 growth.
Consolidated Engineering EBITDA margin expected around 17-18% for H2 FY27 at consolidated level, and about 22% at India level; subject to metal price movements.
Q3 expected to be seasonally soft as large international buyers slow purchases near calendar year-end.
Advantek capex about INR350 crores plus after phase completion, with about INR250 crores of term loans; combined India and China capex of about INR220 crores over 12-15 months, targeted by June 2027.
Romania: aim to arrest operating losses by end FY27; management declined to commit to EBITDA positivity in Q4.

Foreign subsidiaries' combined FY27 loss expected to be a low single-digit crore figure; H2 for Advantek and foreign subsidiaries together expected to be positive, though full-year may still show a minor loss.
capex_capacity: Capex in Q2 was INR35.6 crores; H1 consolidated capex about INR73 crores, of which standalone about INR9 crores.
Advantek expansion (Bushings, Stampings, large Cages) is on track, with production expected in the next few quarters; go-live may take longer due to customer approvals and trials.
China brownfield expansion for steel Cages is scheduled to commence production in Q3 FY28; commercialisation expected around end of H1 FY28.
Maintenance capex at consolidated level about INR25-30 crores per year, including China and Romania sites.
Management noted the incremental specific capex on productive assets is about 2x of revenue potential, with infrastructure capex shared across years.
demand_pricing: Cages: decent demand traction from industrial and automotive in India; export demand strong from Europe, US and Japan. Large-size Cages expected to ramp in H2 FY27, with at least 20% annual growth in that segment.

Resourcing/outsourcing project: commercial sales to begin in Q3 and normalise by Q4 FY27, with peak run-rate about INR70-75 crores per year; a further INR75-100 crores of Cage opportunities from Europe and North America in pipeline.
Japan-based customer Cage growth: H1 up about 28%; management guides 10-15% annual growth.

Metal pass-through: copper and zinc (brass) increases over the last six months partly passed through; pass-through remains ongoing with lag per customer, and indirect cost inflation is not fully recovered.
Management estimates it captures a large share of incremental bearing-capex-driven Cage demand from Indian bearing makers; Cage TAM estimated at about 5% of bearing value.
Aerospace and defence stamping opportunity is small, about INR20-30 crores; a larger stamping opportunity is in other components.

qa_highlights.question: Romania: will operating profitability convert into net profit, and what is the strategy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is too early to confirm net profitability; it is working on cost structure and will update quarterly. Details of downsizing were deferred to about one quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 18.6% margin driven by pass-through or mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said both: some metal pass-through, lower solar contribution, and operational efficiency. India margin was seen as steady around 22%, with consolidated margin of 17-18% for H2.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY27 consolidated guidance only 10-12% after 21% H1 growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited metal inflation, quantitative growth of 12-15%, and Romania downsizing reducing contribution. India guidance is conservative, not an implied slowdown.

qa_highlights.question: What is the capex plan for FY27 and split between Advantek and China?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India capex is about INR110 crores over 1-1.5 years and China about INR100 crores; about INR70 crores spent in H1. Completion targeted by June 2027 with go-live later.

qa_highlights.question: Advantek peak interest and depreciation?
qa_highlights.answer: Combined interest and depreciation around INR7.5-8 crores currently, rising to a maximum of about INR10 crores once fully running; Advantek capex loan about INR250 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Bushing contract delayed and what about large windmills?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Bushing contract commercialisation is slightly delayed but still expected. It is supplying Bushings to a 16 MW windmill application and sees a continued opportunity.

risks_watch: Romania downsizing: cost, headcount, capacity and one-off charges not yet disclosed; management promised clarity in about one quarter.
Metal price volatility (copper, zinc) and lag in pass-through; indirect cost inflation not fully recovered.
Advantek losses: H1 loss about INR7 crores with rising interest and depreciation; full-year profitability uncertain.
China growth at 5-7% for current portfolio and single-digit EBITDA margin until new capacity starts in FY28.
Stamping and Bushing ramp timelines may slip; Bushing contract commercialisation seen as delayed.
Seasonal Q3 softness from calendar-year-end buyers; resourcing project depends on customer approvals and trials.
summary.management_tone: Confident on India Engineering and project pipeline, but cautious and somewhat evasive on Romania downsizing details, Advantek losses and Bushing timelines, deferring specifics to next quarter. Guidance was described as deliberately conservative.
key_quotes: So if I have to summarize our quarter 2 performance in one sentence, I will say it was a business as usual and largely on track.
Harsha India will 100% grow at a higher rate.
So we do not, as of now, assuming incremental borrowings in FY28.
And we are very comfortable at the current debt level.
